env.world: A population BACKSHIFT multi-environment covariance system. Fix a dimension \(p\in\{2,3,\ldots\}\) and a finite label set \(E=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) of observed environment slots, a corruption budget \(c\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}\), and \(h=m-c\). Write \(\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\) and \(\mathbb S_{++}^{p}\) for the real symmetric positive-semidefinite and positive-definite \(p\times p\) cones. An observed input is a family \(\Sigma=(\Sigma_e:e\in E)\in(\mathbb S_{+}^{p})^{E}\). A structural explanation consists of an invertible demixing matrix \(D\in\mathrm{GL}_p(\mathbb R)\) with connectivity target \(B=I_p-D\), an invariant disturbance covariance \(\Omega\in\mathbb S^{p}\) that is permitted to be nondiagonal and singular, and nonnegative diagonal intervention-variance levels \(s=(s_{ek})\) on an unknown honest set \(H\subseteq E\) with \(\lvert H\rvert=h\), linked by the equilibrium covariance equation \(\Sigma_e=D^{-1}(\Omega+\operatorname{diag}(s_e))D^{-\mathsf T}\) for \(e\in H\); the remaining \(c\) slots of \(E\setminus H\) may carry arbitrary elements of \(\mathbb S_{+}^{p}\). Admissibility is the BACKSHIFT normalization \(\mathcal D=\{A\in\mathrm{GL}_p(\mathbb R):\operatorname{diag}(A)=\mathbf 1,\ \operatorname{CP}(I_p-A)<1\}\), where \(\operatorname{CP}\) is the maximum absolute entry product along a directed simple cycle of length at least two. Two competing explanations \(D^{(1)},H_1,s^{(1)}\) and \(D^{(2)},H_2,s^{(2)}\) with \(\lvert H_r\rvert\ge h\) may share only the overlap \(J=H_1\cap H_2\), of size at least \(m-2c=h-c\). The geometry of a shift design is measured by affine lines \(L\subset\mathbb R^2\): the pairwise occupancy \(M_{k\ell}=\max_L\#\{e\in H:(s_{ek},s_{e\ell})\in L\}\), the deletion distance \(\delta_H=\min_{k<\ell}(h-M_{k\ell})\), and the affine-minor separation \(\gamma_H\). The recovery map is the \(c\)-replacement compatibility set \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\subseteq\mathcal D\), with its subset-enumeration presentation \(\text{SubsetConsensus}\). Conditioning margins are \(\kappa_D=\|D\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|D^{-1}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), \(\zeta_D=1-\operatorname{CP}(I_p-D)\), and the scale bound \(M_H=1+\|\Omega\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in H}\|\Sigma_e\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\max_{e\in H}\|\operatorname{diag}(s_e)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\); no interiority margin is imposed on the covariances, which are only required to be positive semidefinite. The size of a set-valued structural output is measured by \(\operatorname{diam}_{\mathrm{op}}\) and \(\operatorname{outer}_{\mathrm{op}}\), both valued in \([0,+\infty]\).

env.world: A prespecified sparse intervention-design genericity world. On a probability space carrying the shift design, a deterministic binary support pattern \(Z\in\{0,1\}^{H\times p}\) is fixed before the experiment, and random positive amplitudes \(a\in(0,\infty)^{H\times p}\) produce the realized shift levels \(s_{ek}=Z_{ek}a_{ek}\). It states no graphical condition, forms no interventional kernel, and has no treatment/outcome pair, so `Identifiable`, `Overlap`, `Adjustment`, `Backdoor.*`, `Frontdoor.*`, `ATE.*`, `DID.*`, `DTR.*`, `LATE.*`, `GraphicalThms.*`, `SWIGGraph` and the whole `PO.*`/`SCM.Do.*` layer have no type-fitting declaration; `Graph/DAG.lean` additionally assumes acyclicity, which this world denies. What IS reused, at exactly the right abstraction, is Causalean's linear-causal-discovery matrix layer — `Causalean.Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.genPerm_of_det_ne_zero_of_colSupport` discharges the monomial-extraction step of the paper's core lemma verbatim. Recorded as `bypass_justified: true` on all three S-blocks with a per-module survey in `file_plan.bypass_survey`.

Both are triaged as build-inline after reading their proofs: each is long (600-800 and ~1100 lines respectively) but every step is elementary and written out, the hardest single step of both has a verbatim Causalean discharge (`genPerm_of_det_ne_zero_of_colSupport`), and the contraction theorem's only Defer-tier ingredients — Heine-Borel and extreme-value attainment — are separately gated and threaded. Deferring either would drop the paper's population core or its analytic endpoint for length rather than for open mathematics, which the triage rule forbids. Two former gates disappear for different reasons: the QE gate because its whole consumer layer left the core, and `lem:randomized-sdc-complete-family-recovery` because the revised core no longer carries it as a node at all (He-Kressner now appears only in the `comparator_promise_table`, which is not a node set). The file plan compensates by pre-splitting both chains across dedicated `Helpers/` files.

decisions.decision: Maximum affine-line occupancy is realized as a `Finset.sup` over collinear INDEX subsets, not as a supremum over affine lines.
decisions.rationale: A sup over the infinite set of affine lines is awkward in Lean and, worse, invites a set-of-points reading that would silently deduplicate the coincident type-\(00\) shift points at the origin — destroying the multiplicity that `prop:generic-support-frontier`'s four-term formula depends on ('This application counts indexed observations, so coincident zero-shift points contribute with their full multiplicity'). Ranging over subsets of the index set \(H\) preserves multiplicity by construction, is total and finite, and matches `def:affine-separation`'s minor-based collinearity criterion, so both consume one shared bridge lemma (a finite indexed family lies on a common affine line iff every triple has vanishing affine minor, the note's own display (16)).

decisions.decision: `def:subset-consensus` is emitted as a set-theoretic union over size-\(h\) subsets, not as an executable oracle-driven solver.
decisions.rationale: The core is explicit that this is a 'definitional implementation note', that neither the \(\binom mh\) query count nor the identity with \(\mathcal R_c(\Sigma)\) is a theorem contribution, and that no encoded terminating solver is supplied. A set-theoretic union keeps the definition faithful to that disclaimer, makes the query count a `Finset.card` fact, and makes the identity a `Set.ext` proved beside the definition rather than an exported claim.

decisions.decision: REVISED (F1.5 review, FLAG-missed-reuse) — `rRadius`, `diamOp` and `outerOp` are all `ℝ≥0∞`-valued, and `diamOp` is now REUSED Mathlib `Metric.ediam` rather than a local functional; only `rRadius` and `outerOp` remain local, and all three are written with `edist` under `open scoped Matrix.Norms.L2Operator`.
decisions.rationale: The `ℝ≥0∞` value type is unchanged and still load-bearing: the core explicitly allows \(+\infty\) for all three ('with value \(+\infty\) allowed', '\(\in[0,+\infty]\)'), and Mathlib's real-valued `Metric.diam` returns 0 on an unbounded set, which would make the contraction hypothesis \(r_{n,\alpha,H}\le r_0\) vacuously satisfiable on an unbounded confidence region — a soundness bug, so `Metric.diam` stays rejected. What changes is the diameter: the previous entry rejected the extended-valued diameter for 'plumbing', citing `EMetric.diam` and a scoped `Matrix.L2OpNorm` instance. Both citations were wrong. The decl is `Metric.ediam` (`Mathlib/Topology/EMetricSpace/Diam.lean:32`), `⨆ (x ∈ s) (y ∈ s), edist x y` over a `PseudoEMetricSpace` — verbatim the core's supremum shape, `ℝ≥0∞`-valued, so it preserves the required infinite value on an unbounded set; the `EMetric.*` spellings are deprecated aliases in the same file, which is why the earlier index search came up empty. And the scope is `Matrix.Norms.L2Operator` (`Mathlib/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/Matrix.lean:172,183`), which exposes `Matrix.instL2OpMetricSpace` alongside the very `Matrix.instL2OpNormedAddCommGroup` this development already opens for `‖·‖` — so the metric structure comes for free with the norm, there is no second instance to plumb, and the only bridge is `edist x y = ENNReal.ofReal ‖x - y‖` by `edist_dist`/`dist_eq_norm`, i.e. simp. Reuse is therefore mandatory under Step 0, and it buys the consumer discharge `Metric.ediam_le` (:53) for free. `rRadius` and `outerOp` stay define-local because Mathlib has no per-index or one-sided sup-of-distances decl (`Metric.infDist`/`EMetric.infEdist` are infima), but they are re-expressed with `edist` in the same ambient structure so the whole `ℝ≥0∞` layer is uniform.

decisions.decision: REVISED — the local contraction radius \(r_0\) is emitted as an EXISTENTIAL, non-effective quantity inside `thm:non-effective-four-margin-contraction`; no constants bundle, no release/abstain handle, and no dyadic search is defined anywhere in the plan.
decisions.rationale: This supersedes the former D-plan-7 (`certificateInferenceHandle`) and D-plan-8 (`Nat.sInf` dyadic \(\underline\mu\)), both of whose definitions were deleted from the core by this revision. The revised core states the radius as 'there exists a real number \(r_0>0\), depending only on \(p,m,c,\gamma_0,\zeta_0,\overline\kappa,\overline M\)' and says in terms that 'The existence of \(r_0\) is non-effective: no procedure is asserted for checking the universal candidate premise or for computing \(r_0\)'. Emitting \(L_0,K_0,\rho_0,C_0\) as ordinary `Real` expressions in the theorem statement (they ARE explicit and closed-form, so they stay in the statement) while binding \(r_0\) by `∃ r₀ > 0, …` is the only encoding faithful to that split: it makes the modulus checkable and the radius honestly non-constructive, and it removes any temptation to expose a `Decidable`/`Option` interface that the core disclaims. The compact family \(\mathfrak T\), its far subfamily, the residual \(\mathfrak r\) and \(\mu_0\) are proof-local objects in `Helpers/ContractionCompactness.lean`, not core nodes, so they need no plan node.

decisions.decision: REVISED — the covariance-interiority margin is removed everywhere, and its role in bounding the candidate nuisance and shifts is taken over by a PSD-summand operator-norm monotonicity helper.
decisions.rationale: The revised core deletes the symbols `lambda`/`lambda0` and the clause \(\Gamma_e\succeq\lambda_0I_p\) from the constraint family, keeping only \(\Omega,\Psi,\Sigma_e,\Gamma_e\in\mathbb S_+^p\). The bound that previously came from interiority now comes from display (17): if \(P,Q\succeq0\) then \(\|P\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\|P+Q\|_{\mathrm{op}}\), applied to \(A\Gamma_eA^{\mathsf T}=\Psi+\operatorname{diag}(t_e)\). F2 must emit that helper in `Helpers/MatrixMargins.lean` and must NOT reintroduce an interiority premise to shortcut it — doing so would silently strengthen the theorem's hypotheses relative to the core, which explicitly closes with 'No candidate affine-separation, normalization-slack, scale, or covariance-interiority condition was used.'

decisions.rationale: The former D-plan-9 governed commentary in the deleted `thm:certified-inference-representation-obstruction`. The same discipline now applies to `thm:non-effective-four-margin-contraction`, whose closing sentences ('The existence of \(r_0\) is non-effective …', 'no executable, algorithmic, or software interface is asserted') are scope commentary: turning them into conjuncts would produce model-independent shells. Everything the deleted layer used to claim is recorded, non-assertively, in the `_root_.List _root_.String` payload of `oeq:certified-uniform-inference`. NO TAUTOLOGICAL CONJUNCTS anywhere: in particular the OEQ's 'possibly using a conservative universal four-margin audit' clause is NOT promoted to a formal audit predicate, since no audit object exists in the revised core.

decisions.decision: NEW (core revision) — `oeq:certified-uniform-inference` is a Case-(B) non-assertive `_root_.List _root_.String` payload, and no delivered theorem depends on it.
decisions.rationale: The revised core turns the former headline into an unresolved open-ended question, which `design_decisions.d0_open_oeq_residuals` records as the note's acknowledged open problem. Every truth condition it asks about — an executable real-closed-field QE/sign-determination/root-isolation substrate, a release-or-abstain decision, a rational empty/singleton/multiple classifier, an effective radius, chart automation, a corruption-aware CRAN extension — is undefined in the revised core, which deleted the entire symbolic layer that used to define them, and the node states in terms that all of it is unresolved future work. Case (A) is therefore unavailable (there is no fully specified predicate to record as a `Prop`), and the carrier must be a descriptive non-`Prop` payload. A `List String` rather than a single `String` is chosen only because the question has four numbered desiderata plus two further asks plus four disclaimers, and one literal per clause keeps the payload legible and makes it obviously change when the question changes; it is still a direct literal of a permitted carrier type, with no selector, procedure, rate, confidence or lower-bound witness field.
